search-summaries.name: Search summaries of Vinous (Antonio Galloni) and Jeb Dunnuck on Napa 2019
search-summaries.note: Relayed through a search summary. The Vinous and Dunnuck pages were not read.

claims.claim: The year began with heavy rain, and the soil kept its moisture late into the season.
claims.note: Wine Independent puts January to May rainfall at just over 34 inches, against 0.61 inches in 2018.

claims.claim: After the wet spring, the season was dry and sunny. Summer was long and warm with foggy mornings. Extreme heat was rare.
It was a warmer year than 2018: 3,240 growing degree days against 3,050.
Whites came in from late September, after a cooler mid-September with some rain. Reds ripened in sunny days and cool nights in October. Harvest wrapped up by mid-November.
claims.note: One source. Wine Independent says harvest ran from early September to late October.

claims.claim: Napa County red grape tonnage was 121,100 tons in 2019, down from 137,335 tons in 2018.
claims.note: Wine Independent cites the Napa County crop report. The crop report itself was not read.

claims.claim: Yields were average to slightly below average.
claims.note: Wine Independent calls them slightly above average per vine for growers who cut back, but the county tonnage is lower. See conflicts.

claims.claim: The wines are fruit-forward and generous, with plush tannins, more alcohol and less acidity than 2018. Many reds are 14.5 to 14.9%.
claims.quote: The hallmark of 2019 is firmly on the fruit
claims.note: One source. Harvest Napa says instead that the fruit kept bright acidity and soft tannins.

claims.claim: Winemakers reported deeper color than expected. The long, mild finish to the season kept freshness and gave soft tannins.
Vinous called the Cabernets big, bold wines that show the extroverted side of Napa. It found the vintage less consistent than 2018.
claims.quote: big, bold wines that show the extroverted side of Napa Valley

claims.claim: Jeb Dunnuck called 2019 another terrific year, ranking it below 2016 and 2013.
Structured 2019 reds may age 25 to 35 years or more.
claims.note: One source, and it refers to the best structured wines, not Napa as a whole.

conflicts: Yields: Harvest Napa says average to slightly below average. Wine Independent says growers were more conservative than in 2018 and landed at slightly above-average levels. County red tonnage fell about 12% from 2018.
Acidity: Harvest Napa says bright acidity. Wine Independent says less acidity than 2018. Both can be true (bright for the year, lower than 2018).
Harvest start: early September (Wine Independent) against late September for whites and October for reds (Harvest Napa).
gaps: No Napa Valley Vintners or UC Davis report read directly.
The Vinous and Dunnuck pages were not read, only summaries.
No Atlas Peak or mountain-specific note on 2019. The sheet line is valley-wide.
Fine+Rare and James Suckling vintage pages were found but not read.

sheet.vintage: A wet winter and spring, then a long, dry, warm summer. The reds are ripe and fruit-forward, with soft tannins.
